author: Shanon Adame
title: Alcoa Middle students see themselves on screen - NewsBreak
text:
By Shanon Adame ,
5 hours ago
Alcoa Middle School students got to see themselves on the big screen Dec. 3 after acting in background roles for an area filmmaker.
Director Matt Webb came to the Alcoa campus in August to film his short, “Used to Be,” using AMS performing arts students as extras in a dodgeball scene . Those students got a first-hand look into the film industry after spending about 12 hours on set.
The film was a collaborative project between Matt and his daughter, Ally Webb, who helped write the script.
“Used to Be” tackles themes of anxiety and is based on Ally’s childhood struggle with emetophobia, the fear of vomiting.
Matt and Ally entered the film into Film Fest Knox’s Elev8tor Pitch competition and won third place.
The competition is aimed at short films that have potential to be turned into feature-length films.
On Dec. 3, Matt, Ally and Thomson Nguyen, director of photography, dropped by Alcoa Middle School to visit the students who acted in their film, some of whom hadn’t yet seen it.
After showing the eight-minute film, the film crew opened up the room for questions and discussion.
Students had already submitted some pre-thought-out questions, but many asked questions on the fly, after seeing the film.
The students talked about what they expected and what surprised them about the film. One student said some aspects of the film had a creepy overtone, something he wouldn’t have predicted during filming.
Being able to identify areas of their school that ended up in the film also caused some excitement from the group.
Other questions ranged from how Matt found the cast members to how they would rework the film if they had unlimited funds.
“More people and more equipment,” Nguyen answered.
Then the discussion turned to mental health.
One student asked about the main character’s phobia, emetophobia.
“I know it seems kind of stupid, but it affects my life a lot and affected my life a lot in middle school; I would get made fun of for it, and so that’s what the movie was about,” Ally told the student.
One popular question the students had was whether they would get the chance to act in a full-length version of the film. Unfortunately for those hopeful actors, by the time Matt could start filming, the students would be too old to reprise their prior roles.
For now, the film will make its way to different film festivals around the United States, and Matt and crew, Scruffy Media Partners, will go through mentoring and workshops with industry professionals to turn their eight-minute film into a feature-length length film.
